oneLiner: The custom-ASIC arms dealer at escape velocity: AI revenue $16.7B in a single quarter, FY2026 tracking ~$58B, and management now guiding FY2027 to ~$115B and FY2028 to ~$230B with supply already secured.
thesis: Six XPU customers anchor the model, four of them material: Google (Ironwood TPU v7 in volume, TPU v8i now in production), Anthropic, OpenAI (first-generation 'Jalapeno' shipping), and Meta (MTIA).

Management guided AI semiconductor revenue to roughly $115B in FY2027 and $230B in FY2028 - about $350B of AI silicon over two years, with supply secured for both - and said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 of EPS in FY2028.

Networking grows as fast as XPUs: Tomahawk 6 is the fastest switch ramp in company history and nearly sold out, Tomahawk 7 (first 200 Tbps Ethernet switch) has taped out, and Tomahawk Ultra brings scale-up inside the rack onto Ethernet.
Infrastructure software reaccelerated to +29% YoY at 94% gross margin and ~84% operating margin with ARR +15%: VMware funds the AI build-out from internal cash.

latestQuarter.label: Q3 FY2026 (ended Aug 2, 2026; reported Sep 2, 2026)
points: AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY and +54% QoQ - 56% of total revenue vs 49% in Q2; XPUs were 73% of AI revenue and shipped up 3.5x YoY, AI networking up 2.5x.
Non-GAAP gross margin 75.0% (down 210bp QoQ, above the 74% guide); record non-GAAP operating margin 67.9% (+240bp YoY); EPS $3.32 (+96%); GAAP EPS $2.68.
FCF a record $13.67B, 46% of revenue, on just $532M of capex; non-AI semis $4.2B (+5% YoY, flat QoQ).
Balance sheet: $24.0B cash, $59.6B gross fixed-rate debt at a 4% weighted coupon and 7.4-year average maturity; $5.6B repaid in the quarter, no buybacks.

segments: Semiconductor solutions 70% of revenue (was 57% a year ago): custom XPUs, Tomahawk AI networking, PCIe switching, optical DSPs and lasers, wireless, broadband, storage. Segment operating margin 61%, up 440bp YoY.

Infrastructure software 30%: VMware, mainframe, security. 94% gross margin, ~84% operating margin (+650bp YoY), ARR +15%. VMware Private AI Cloud is the new enterprise-AI attach and the workload-repatriation pitch.
competitive: NVIDIA is still the pricing umbrella, but Broadcom claims an XPU co-designed to one lab's workload matches Rubin-class GPUs at less than half the cost, and puts its own content at $20-30B per gigawatt versus the ~$40B analysts ascribe to NVIDIA.
Marvell competes for custom co-design sockets; management pointed to shipping Google's TPU v8i ahead of MediaTek's V8T as proof of time-to-market advantage.

The binding constraints are physical, not commercial: substrates, leading-edge wafers, HBM, and customer land/power/shell. Broadcom is standing up its own Singapore substrate fab in FY2027 and more than tripling indium-phosphide EML/CW/VCSEL laser capacity.
VMware alternatives (Nutanix, Proxmox, hyperscaler-native) still circle the installed base, but +29% growth and 15% ARR growth say the repricing is holding.
moat: Multi-generation, multi-gigawatt co-design contracts institutionalize the customer relationships years ahead of revenue: a new long-term Google agreement for multiple tens of billions of dollars of TPUs annually, Anthropic at 1GW in 2026 scaling to 5GW in 2027 with line of sight to 10GW more in 2028, OpenAI at 1.3GW in 2027 and over 5GW in 2028, Meta at 3GW through 2028. Underneath sit SerDes, chip-to-chip interconnect, HBM and SRAM integration and advanced packaging IP, plus the industry's fastest definition-to-production record with no respins. Ethernet switching leadership means Broadcom monetizes the cluster even where it does not supply the accelerator.
risks: The FY27/FY28 outlook is now the stock: $115B and $230B leave no margin for error, and deployment timing depends on customers' land, power and shell, not on Broadcom's silicon.
Extreme customer concentration: Anthropic becomes the largest XPU customer in 2027 and OpenAI the second largest in 2028 - both pre-profit AI labs whose funding is not yet self-sustaining.

Vendor-financing optics: the XPV platform with Apollo and Blackstone targets more than 20GW for OpenAI and Anthropic by end-2028; the first $35B tranche closed in June, and prior filings disclosed roughly $29B of maximum exposure with modest residual-value guarantees.
Gross margin is structurally declining - guided to ~73% in Q4 from 78% a year ago - as XPU memory content rises; only operating leverage keeps operating margin flat at ~66%.
Supply, not demand, caps the outlook. Management says demand exceeds even the $115B FY27 number, which means the guide is a supply forecast dressed as a demand forecast.
Guide-versus-consensus risk is chronic: two consecutive quarters have beaten on the print and sold off on the next quarter's guide.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 and full-year results Dec 9, 2026 - the first hard check on the $115B FY2027 path.
Goldman Sachs Communacopia and Technology conference Sept 8, 2026.
Tomahawk 7 sampling and Tomahawk Ultra scale-up deployments through FY2027.
Additional XPV tranches for OpenAI and Anthropic; an Anthropic IPO would change the counterparty credit picture.
Singapore substrate fab entering production in FY2027, the stated relief valve on the supply bottleneck.
pricedIn: About $357 is roughly 28% below the $495 52-week high even as AI revenue tripled year over year - near 60x trailing but only ~18x forward earnings, among the cheapest forward multiples in the AI complex. The market is explicitly declining to pay for FY2028. The debate is binary: if $230B of FY2028 AI revenue and more than $30 of EPS are real, the stock trades near 12x that number and everything else is noise; if the labs' funding, power or data-center shells slip even a year, the same guidance becomes the most expensive promise in semiconductors.

scenarios.bear: Deployment, not demand, is what bites: Anthropic and OpenAI shells and power slip, XPV tranches get harder to place on acceptable terms, one hyperscaler dual-sources a generation, and FY2027 AI lands nearer $90B than $115B. Gross margin keeps sliding on memory content while opex catches up; the market marks the FY2028 target to zero and the stock revisits the high-$200s.
scenarios.base: FY2026 closes near $58B of AI revenue; FY2027 tracks to roughly $115B on Google TPU v8i volume, Anthropic's 5GW and OpenAI's 1.3GW; software holds mid-20s growth; operating margin stays near 66% as leverage offsets mix dilution. EPS compounds fast enough that even a flat multiple carries the stock back toward the mid-$400s.
scenarios.bull: The gigawatt math converts: most of the roughly 30GW of customer demand across FY2027-28 actually deploys, FY2028 clears $230B, EPS exceeds $30, and Ethernet scale-up plus in-house optics widen content per rack. At even 15x forward, that is a materially higher stock, and the second pillar of AI silicon re-rates toward NVIDIA's terms.

valPresets.note: FCF is compounding violently: $13.7B in Q3 FY2026 alone and $31.9B across three quarters versus $19.4B a year earlier. The base preset (40% year-1, fading) is consistent with the ~$115B FY2027 AI path; the bull preset tracks the $230B FY2028 outlook.

latestProse: Q3 FY2026 (ended Aug 2; reported Sep 2). Revenue $29.59B, +86% YoY: semiconductors $20.84B (+127%), infrastructure software $8.75B (+29%). AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY and +54% sequentially, now 56% of total revenue versus 49% in Q2; XPU shipments rose 3.5x YoY and were 73% of AI revenue, with networking up 2.5x. Non-GAAP gross margin 75.0%, record non-GAAP operating margin 67.9%, EPS $3.32 (+96%), free cash flow $13.67B on $532M of capex. The disclosure that matters most: gross margin fell 210bp sequentially while operating margin hit a record - XPU memory content is diluting cost of goods exactly as management warned, and only operating leverage is offsetting it.
guidanceProse: Q4 guide is $34.8B (+93% YoY) against roughly $35.0B consensus - the second straight quarter where a clear beat was overshadowed by an in-line-to-light guide; the stock closed Sep 2 at $367.24 and fell about 5% after hours. Inside it: semis $26.1B (+136%), AI semis $21.7B (+236%), software $8.7B (+25%), gross margin ~73% versus 78% a year ago, operating margin ~66% (flat YoY), capex $1.4B. FY2026 AI revenue was raised to about $58B (+186%) from ~$56B. Management then guided FY2027 AI revenue to roughly $115B and FY2028 to roughly $230B - about $350B over two years, with supply secured for both - and said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 of EPS in fiscal 2028.
